release.verification: Entire original HDF5 in 192 HTTP 206 byte ranges; per-response Content-Range and lengths checked, full-file MD5 matched repository, SHA-256 locally computed. Other distribution AURSAD.pkl omitted.

evidence_level: downloaded original measurement file and read full paper; all 6,249,074 rows processed.
hardware_and_recording: Real UR3e arm and OnRobot screwdriving tool, nominally sampled at 100 Hz. Register relay on a separate URScript thread and common RTDE stream through the robot controller as described in Section 4.2. Appendix A documents problems with direct screwdriver acquisition. Signals share published rows; no separately verified device-level latency correction is applied.

fields.sample_nr_and_label: Contiguous equal pairs define a segment; sample numbers and CSV row ranges allow independent extraction. Labels 0–4 are assembly observations, 5 = auxiliary loosening or picking.
fields.spindle: output_double_register_24/25/26 = achieved, current and target torque in N m, respectively. Achieved can hold a prior result. Peaks are maxima of absolute values.
fields.tcp: Euclidean norm of actual_TCP_force_3..5 (rotational wrench channels, N m). The three-axis resultant at the TCP is frame- and load-dependent, and differs physically from axial spindle torque.
fields.status: output_bit_register_67 = tightening, 70 = driver busy, 71 = process not OK and 72 = OK. In this release bit 67 is a short pulse rather than a sustained operation interval. The primary active window selects bit 70 within assembly events (labels 0–4). The intersection of bits 67 and 70 is reported separately as a diagnostic.
fields.threshold: A threshold attainment in the summaries means at least one active row with a strictly positive setpoint and abs(current torque) >= target torque. No interpolation or timing claim is used.
fields.clock: Output t_first_s/t_last_s are controller timestamps; clock checks exclude event boundaries. Nominal step is 10 ms.

limits: The release does not provide an independently calibrated in-line torque reference, clamp/preload measurement or a timestamped physical seat-contact label. A spindle register crossing or an OK bit cannot establish preload or seating independently.

Normal and anomaly labels refer to entire events. Missing-screw events include induced omissions and actual pick-up failures without separate labels (Section 5.1). Damaged plate thread has only three samples.

The extra assembly component is an added washer. The auxiliary class is not a sixth tightening outcome. The data does not justify comparison of TCP-moment magnitude to a signed drive-axis moment without frame, alignment and load treatment.
reproduce: Using NumPy and h5py, run python derive_aursad.py AURSAD.h5 OUTPUT_DIR. Event classes, conditional peak extrema (N m), and threshold counts are in screwdriver-events-by-label.csv. screwdriver-segments.csv records half-open source row ranges and per-segment flags and extrema.
findings: In busy rows of labeled tightening events the instantaneous absolute spindle torque reached the positive target at least once in 616 of 1,420 normal, 51 of 221 damaged-screw, 28 of 183 extra-component, 4 of 218 missing-screw, and 1 of 3 damaged-thread events. A positive threshold occurrence is neither necessary for the normal class nor sufficient to reject a missing-screw event in these observations.

Process OK bit 72 and process not OK bit 71 remained zero across all recorded rows. Bit 67 appeared only on 2,039 rows; just 62 of those also had busy bit 70. Explicitly time-matched manual seat labels cannot be obtained from these flags.
validation: Both derived CSVs were regenerated twice and byte-compared. An independent NumPy memory map of native HDF5 blocks checked per-class sample counts, row counts, events with active busy bits, events reaching positive target torque, OK and not-OK. All six label groups agreed.
